subject: Dedicated capacity delivery runway and gating plan
messages:
From: Maya Rao <ops@novasystems.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity discussion — initial asks

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To move from POC to a reserved GPU pool we need a clear gating plan that ties technical milestones to procurement milestones. Key constraints from our side:
- We need 24/7 availability for inference (strict SLOs) starting mid-July.
- Preferred regions: us-west-2 primary, fallback in eu-west-1.
- Target steady-state: 8x A100-class GPUs (can be mixed with A10s for cost) with burst to 16 for peak windows.
- Procurement lead: 3–4 weeks after final SOW; legal wants a clear cutover checklist.

Can you share a delivery runway (stages, gating criteria, who signs off at each gate) plus a tentative procurement timeline we can pass to Contracts?

Thanks — attaching our internal draft intake for visibility.

Maya
VP, Infrastructure
Novasystems
Attachments: novas_intake_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <ops@novasystems.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity delivery runway and gating plan

Maya — appreciate the detail.

I put together a first-pass runway and gating checklist (attached). High level:
1) Stage 0 — Intake & alignment (now–May 21): capacity profile, target regions, compliance checklist.
   - Sign-off: Novasystems infra + Redwood CS director (kimberly).
2) Stage 1 — Staging deployment & perf validation (May 22–June 11): deploy a mirrored staging pool in us-west-2, run 72-hour soak tests with realistic traffic and KV-cache priming.
   - Gate criteria: 95th perc latency < 120ms for 2k qps profile, stable memory footprint.
3) Stage 2 — Procurement & reserved capacity commit (June 12–July 2): finalize SOW, PO, and reserved nodes.
   - Procurement milestone: PO issued by June 25 to hit mid-July cutover.
4) Stage 3 — Production cutover & warm-up (July 3–July 17): gradual traffic shift with automatic fallback rules.

Notes on burst: we recommend a two-tier burst policy — "warm burst" (same pool, extra pre-warmed A10s) for predictable peaks, and "cold burst" (cross-region fallbacks or on-demand cloud GPUs) for extreme traffic. We include autoscale hysteresis to avoid flapping and a circuit-breaker that will failover to a cheaper model variant if latency exceeds thresholds.

I've attached delivery_runway_v1.xlsx. Kimberly, can you confirm the staging acceptance tests and hardware-family constraints? Ben — I'm looping you for procurement cadence and terms discussion.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachments: delivery_runway_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rao <ops@novasystems.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity delivery runway and gating plan

+1 on Markus' outline — a few technical clarifications to ensure staging mirrors production traffic: 
- GPU families: staging should use 4x A100 (40GB) and 4x A10 for the steady-state mix; we will tag instances so runtime picks quantization-optimized kernels for A10 where available.
- KV cache warm-up: we'll provide a priming script (small dataset) to ensure KV hit rate > 70% before load testing.
- Autoscale policy: min=8, target=8, warm_burst=+4 (pre-warmed A10s), cold_burst=+8 (on-demand cross-region). Warm burst should have a 3-minute scale-up window; cold burst requires manual approval from Novasystems ops or an automated policy triggered by sustained 5-minute CPU/GPU queue depth.

I've added acceptance test rows to the attached delivery_runway_v1.xlsx (see tab "staging_acceptance"). Maya — can your ops team confirm they can run the soak traffic window (we'll supply the load harness)?

-Kimberly
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Rao <ops@novasystems.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <contracts@novasystems.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity delivery runway and gating plan

Thanks, Kimberly and Markus. This is exactly the level of detail our legal and procurement teams need. Two quick updates from our side:
- We can commit to running the 72-hour soak during the week of May 24. Ops will need the load harness and the priming script by May 20.
- Procurement: Jordan confirms we can issue a provisional PO the week of June 21, final PO by June 28 pending SOW redlines. I've attached a PO stub with our internal billing code and tentative PO window.

One ask: for the cold_burst plan, can Redwood provide an explicit fallback model variant name we will route to (so our internal devs can test correctness)? If not, any suggestions for a cheap, fast-fail variant we can include in our chaos tests?

I'll also schedule a 30-minute sync for Thursday to align milestones.

Maya
Attachments: po_stub.pdf (pdf), novas_intake_v2.xlsx (re-sent)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <ops@novasystems.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity delivery runway and gating plan

Thanks team — confirming:
- Redwood will provide the load harness and priming script by EOD 2027-05-20.
- We'll put a recommended cold_burst fallback (gpt-medium-q4b) — low-cost quantized variant — and document expected output deltas.
- Procurement owner (Ben Carter) will follow up with Jordan for PO flow and will push to lock provisional PO week of June 21.

I'll send an updated timeline after the Thursday sync.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
